questions.question:
Consider the following system of equations:
3x + 2y = 1
4x + 7z = 1
x + y + z = 3
x - 2y + 7z = 0
The number of solutions for this system is
questions.explanation:
Solve the first three equations: from 3x + 2y = 1 and 4x + 7z = 1, substitute into x + y + z = 3: x = [latex]-[/latex]2.2, y = 3.8, z = 1.4.

Check the 4th equation: [latex]-[/latex]2.2 [latex]-[/latex] 7.6 + 9.8 = 0 True. So the system is consistent with exactly one solution.

Answer: 1

questions.question:
Let X be a square matrix. Consider the following two statements on X.

I. X is invertible
II. Determinant of X is non-zero

Which one of the following is TRUE?

options.A: I implies II; II does not imply I
options.B: II implies I; I does not imply II
options.C: I does not imply II; II does not imply I
options.D: I and II are equivalent statements

questions.explanation:
A square matrix is invertible if and only if its determinant is non-zero ([latex]X^{-1}=\frac{adj(X)}{\det X}[/latex]). So I and II imply each other.

Answer: I and II are equivalent statements

questions.question:
Consider the system of linear equations given below.

[latex] \begin{array}{c} a x+y=b \\ 16 x+a y=24 \end{array} [/latex]

Suppose the values of [latex]a[/latex] and [latex]b[/latex] are chosen such that the system of linear equations produce multiple solutions. Then the product of [latex]a[/latex] and [latex]b[/latex] is ________. (answer in integer)
questions.explanation:
The system [latex]ax+y=b,\ 16x+ay=24[/latex] has infinitely many (multiple) solutions exactly when the two equations describe the same line, i.e. all three coefficient ratios are equal:
[latex]\dfrac{a}{16}=\dfrac{1}{a}=\dfrac{b}{24}[/latex]

From [latex]\dfrac{a}{16}=\dfrac{1}{a}[/latex]: [latex]a^2=16\Rightarrow a=\pm4[/latex].
From [latex]\dfrac{1}{a}=\dfrac{b}{24}[/latex]: [latex]b=\dfrac{24}{a}[/latex].

If [latex]a=4[/latex]: [latex]b=24/4=6[/latex], so [latex]ab=4\times6=24[/latex].
If [latex]a=-4[/latex]: [latex]b=24/(-4)=-6[/latex], so [latex]ab=(-4)\times(-6)=24[/latex].

Either valid choice of [latex]a[/latex] gives the same product.

Answer: 24

The value of the following limit is _____
[latex] \lim_{x \to 0+} \frac{ \sqrt{x}}{1-e^{2 \sqrt{x}}}[/latex]

Since [latex]e^{2t}\approx1+2t[/latex]: [latex]\frac{t}{1-e^{2t}}\approx\frac{t}{-2t}=-\frac12[/latex] (same by L'Hospital: [latex]\frac{1}{-2e^{2t}}\to-\frac12[/latex]).

Answer: -0.5

questions.question: For [latex]n>1[/latex], the maximum multiplicity of any eigenvalue of an [latex]n \times n[/latex] matrix with elements from [latex]\mathbb{R}[/latex] is
questions.explanation:
For an [latex]n\times n[/latex] real matrix, the multiplicity of any eigenvalue (as a root of the characteristic polynomial, which has degree [latex]n[/latex]) can be at most [latex]n[/latex].

This bound is achieved: for example, the identity matrix [latex]I_n[/latex] (or any scalar matrix [latex]cI_n[/latex]) has the single eigenvalue [latex]c[/latex] repeated exactly [latex]n[/latex] times.

So the maximum possible multiplicity of any eigenvalue is [latex]n[/latex].

Answer: n

questions.question: Let u and v be two vectors in [latex]R^{2}[/latex] whose Euclidean norms satisfy ||u||=2|| v|| . What is the value of [latex]\alpha[/latex] such that w=u+[latex]\alpha[/latex]v bisects the angle between u and v ?
questions.explanation:
The bisector points along the sum of the unit vectors: [latex]\frac{u}{\|u\|}+\frac{v}{\|v\|}=\frac{u}{2\|v\|}+\frac{v}{\|v\|}=\frac{1}{2\|v\|}(u+2v)[/latex].

So w = u + 2v bisects the angle: [latex]\alpha=2[/latex].

Answer: 2

questions.question:
Consider a function [latex]f : (0,1) \rightarrow \{0,1\}[/latex] defined as follows.

For a real number [latex]r \in (0,1)[/latex], [latex]f(r) = 1[/latex] if the second digit after the decimal point in [latex]r[/latex] is one of the four digits [latex]2, 3, 6,[/latex] and [latex]7[/latex]. Otherwise, [latex]f(r)[/latex] is equal to [latex]0[/latex].

The number of points in [latex](0,1)[/latex] at which [latex]f[/latex] is discontinuous is ______. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanation:
[latex]f(r)[/latex] depends only on the second digit after the decimal point of [latex]r[/latex]. So [latex](0,1)[/latex] is effectively divided into [latex]100[/latex] equal sub-intervals of length [latex]0.01[/latex] (one for each combination of the first two decimal digits), and [latex]f[/latex] is constant throughout each sub-interval, jumping only at the [latex]99[/latex] internal boundary points [latex]r=0.01,0.02,\ldots,0.99[/latex] (a discontinuity occurs at a boundary only if [latex]f[/latex]'s value actually changes across it, i.e. the second digit switches between the "special" set [latex]\{2,3,6,7\}[/latex] and the rest).

Within any fixed first digit, as the second digit cycles [latex]0,1,2,\ldots,9[/latex], the pattern of "special vs. non-special" is: N,N,S,S,N,N,S,S,N,N. Checking each of the [latex]9[/latex] consecutive transitions within this block ([latex]0|1,1|2,\ldots,8|9[/latex]): the value actually changes at [latex]1|2,\ 3|4,\ 5|6,[/latex] and [latex]7|8[/latex] (four changes), while it stays the same at the other five transitions (including the wrap from [latex]9[/latex] to the next first-digit's [latex]0[/latex], since both are non-special).

So each of the [latex]10[/latex] first-digit blocks contributes exactly [latex]4[/latex] genuine discontinuities, and the wrap-around boundaries between blocks never add any more (non-special to non-special). Total discontinuities [latex]=10\times4=40[/latex].

Answer: 40

questions.question: Given [latex]i=\sqrt{-1}[/latex], what will be the evaluation of the definite integral [latex]\int_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{cosx + i sinx}{cosx -i sinx} dx[/latex]?

[latex]\int_0^{\pi/2}e^{2ix}dx=\frac{e^{i\pi}-1}{2i}=\frac{-2}{2i}=-\frac1i=i[/latex]

Answer: i

questions.question: Which one of the following well-formed formulae in predicate calculus is NOT valid?

options.A: [latex](\forall x p(x)\Rightarrow \forall xq(x))\Rightarrow (\exists x\neg p(x) \vee \forall xq(x))[/latex]
options.D: [latex]\forall x (p(x)\vee q(x))\Rightarrow (\forall x p(x) \vee \forall x q(x)) [/latex]

questions.explanation:
Option 4 is not valid: take a domain {1, 2} with p(1), q(2) true and p(2), q(1) false. Then every x satisfies p(x) [latex]\vee[/latex] q(x), but neither "all p" nor "all q" holds.

Options 1-3 are standard valid implications.

Answer: Option 4

questions.question: The coefficient of [latex]x^{12}[/latex] in [latex](x^{3}+x^{4}+x^{5}+x^{6}+. . . )^{3}[/latex] is ______.

Answer: 10

questions.question: The secant method is used to find the root of an equation f(x)=0. It is started from two distinct estimates [latex]x_{a}[/latex] and [latex]x_{b}[/latex] for the root. It is an iterative procedure involving linear interpolation to a root. The iteration stops if [latex]f(x_{b})[/latex] is very small and then [latex]x_{b}[/latex] is the solution. The procedure is given below. Observe that there is an expression which is missing and is marked by ?. Which is the suitable expression that is to be put in place of ? so that it follows all steps of the secant method?
questions.explanation:
The secant line through [latex](x_a,f(x_a))[/latex] and [latex](x_b,f_b)[/latex] crosses the x-axis at:

[latex]x_t=x_b-\frac{(x_b-x_a)f_b}{f_b-f(x_a)}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]x_b-(x_b-x_a)f_b/(f_b-f(x_a))[/latex]
